column1: YAML: what are the three node kinds?
column2:
Everything is one of three, nested arbitrarily:
  scalar   - a single value (string/number/bool/null)
  sequence - an ordered list
  mapping  - key -> value pairs

Two spellings of the same data:
  BLOCK - indentation + dashes (multi-line; what Compose/Actions use)
  FLOW  - inline, JSON-like:  [] = sequence,  {} = mapping
Any JSON is valid flow-style YAML (YAML 1.2 is a superset of JSON).

column1: YAML: anchor (&) vs alias (*) vs merge key (<<)?
column2:
&name  = ANCHOR: label a node
*name  = ALIAS: reuse that labeled node
<<: *name = MERGE the aliased mapping's keys into this one
YAML's built-in DRY (common in docker-compose).
=> a value STARTING with * is an alias -> must be quoted if literal.

column1: YAML: what does a tag (!) do?
column2:
An explicit TYPE override of YAML's implicit typing.
  !!str 8080  forces a string;  !!int / !!bool likewise.
Tools define custom tags (CloudFormation !Ref, !GetAtt).
=> a value STARTING with ! is a tag -> must be quoted if literal.

column1: YAML: the "Norway problem" / implicit typing gotcha?
column2:
Unquoted scalars are auto-typed, sometimes surprisingly:
  NO   -> boolean false (Norway!)     yes/on/y/n -> true/false (YAML 1.1)
  1.10 -> float 1.1 (trailing 0 lost) 01234 -> leading zero may drop
Fix: QUOTE anything you mean as a literal string ("NO", "1.10").

column1: YAML: when must you quote a value?
column2:
When it STARTS with a syntax token, or to defuse implicit typing:
  *  alias    &  anchor    !  tag    [ or {  flow collection    ? : -  (in places)
Unquoted -> parse error / mis-type. Quote -> literal string.
